vocabulary.meaning_en: a piece of work that someone gives you to do
vocabulary.example: My new assignment is to write about the city park.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to give something to many people
vocabulary.note_ar: فعل منفصل: give the papers out
vocabulary.example: The teacher gave out the tests.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to accept a job or a responsibility
vocabulary.example: She is ready to take on a bigger job.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to return to a place or an activity
vocabulary.example: After lunch, we went back to work.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to work together with someone
vocabulary.example: I teamed up with my brother to clean the house.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a person who works well with other people
vocabulary.example: Our manager wants a team player.

vocabulary.meaning_en: happy and positive
vocabulary.example: She is always cheerful in the morning.

vocabulary.meaning_en: someone who likes being with and talking to people
vocabulary.example: A good waiter is a people person.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to pull paper into small pieces
vocabulary.example: He tore up the old letter.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to put something in the trash
vocabulary.example: Please throw away these old papers.

vocabulary.meaning_en: short notices in a newspaper about jobs
vocabulary.example: He reads the want ads every day.

vocabulary.meaning_en: a word game with squares you fill with letters
vocabulary.example: My grandfather does the crossword puzzle every morning.

vocabulary.meaning_en: when a company says it wants to give you a job
vocabulary.example: She got a job offer from a bank.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to present a show on TV or radio
vocabulary.note_en: Also a noun: the host of the show.
vocabulary.example: Anna will host a talk show.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to enter a room or building
vocabulary.example: Thanks for coming in today.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to learn a fact or information
vocabulary.example: I need to find out the time of the meeting.

vocabulary.meaning_en: things you can do well because you learned them
vocabulary.note_en: personal skills = how you work with people
vocabulary.example: This job needs good computer skills.

vocabulary.meaning_en: telling the truth
vocabulary.example: Please give me an honest answer.

vocabulary.meaning_en: feeling happy about something good you did
vocabulary.example: I am proud of my son.

vocabulary.meaning_en: in a bad mood; unhappy and not friendly
vocabulary.example: He is grumpy before his morning coffee.

vocabulary.meaning_en: to do something special for a happy event
vocabulary.example: Let's celebrate your new job!

fine_lines.title: Separable vs inseparable two-word verbs
fine_lines.explanation_ar: بعض الأفعال المركّبة يمكن فصلها ووضع المفعول به في الوسط (throw the paper away، give the tests out). وبعضها لا يُفصل أبدًا (go back، come in). وإذا كان المفعول به ضميرًا مع فعل منفصل، يجب وضعه في الوسط: throw it away وليس throw away it.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Some two-word verbs can come apart, with the object in the middle (throw the paper away, give the tests out). Others always stay together (go back, come in). With a pronoun, a separable verb must come apart: throw it away, not throw away it.

examples.sentence: She threw the old box away.
We went back home at six.

fine_lines.title: cheerful vs grumpy
fine_lines.explanation_ar: cheerful تعني مرحًا ومبتسمًا، و grumpy تعني متضايقًا وغير ودود. في الدرس آنا cheerful وبيت grumpy.
fine_lines.explanation_en: Cheerful means happy and smiling. Grumpy means in a bad mood. In the lesson, Anna is cheerful and Pete is grumpy.

examples.sentence: The cheerful nurse smiled at everyone.
I feel grumpy when I am tired.

expressions.meaning_en: Hope that things go well for me.
expressions.example: I have my test today. Wish me luck!
Lunch at noon? That sounds great.
You said 'different'. What do you mean?

expressions.meaning_en: Go on, tell me; I am paying attention.
expressions.example: You have an idea? I'm listening.
Don't worry about the interview. Just be yourself.

expressions.meaning_en: A polite way to thank someone for a chance.
expressions.example: Thanks for the opportunity to work here.
Okay, I've heard enough. You can go.

expressions.meaning_en: I was sure this would happen.

grammar.title: Phrasal (two-word) verbs
grammar.explanation_ar: الفعل المركّب = فعل + كلمة صغيرة (out, up, back, away, in, on). المعنى الجديد يختلف أحيانًا عن معنى الفعل وحده: give = يعطي، give out = يوزّع. بعض هذه الأفعال يُفصل (give the assignments out) وبعضها لا يُفصل (go back). وإذا كان المفعول به ضميرًا (it, them) نضعه بين الكلمتين: tear them up.
grammar.explanation_en: A phrasal verb is a verb + a small word (out, up, back, away, in, on). The meaning can be new: give = hand something, give out = give to many people. Some can come apart (give the assignments out); some stay together (go back). With a pronoun (it, them), put it in the middle: tear them up.
examples: You can tear these ads up.
I want to go back to hosting.
I need to find out about your skills.

questions.question: What does 'team up' mean?
questions.explanation_ar: team up تعني أن يعمل شخصان أو أكثر معًا.
questions.explanation_en: Team up means to work together with someone.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation_ar: مع الضمير it يجب فصل الفعل: throw it away.
questions.explanation_en: With a pronoun, the phrasal verb must come apart: throw it away.

questions.question: Anna is happy and friendly. She is ____.
Which phrasal verb can NOT come apart?
questions.explanation_ar: go back لا يُفصل: نقول go back to work.

questions.question: 'Wish me luck' means:
choices: Hope things go well for me.
questions.explanation_ar: نقولها قبل أمر صعب مثل امتحان أو مقابلة.
questions.explanation_en: We say it before something hard, like a test or interview.

questions.question: The teacher ____ the tests at 9 o'clock.
questions.explanation_ar: give out تعني يوزّع على الجميع.
questions.explanation_en: Give out means to give something to many people.

questions.question: Someone who likes talking with people is a ____.
questions.explanation_en: A people person enjoys being with people.

questions.question: What does 'find out' mean?
questions.explanation_ar: find out تعني يعرف أو يكتشف معلومة.
questions.explanation_en: Find out means to learn a fact or information.

questions.question: Pete is not friendly and is often in a bad mood. He is ____.
questions.explanation_ar: grumpy تعني متجهّمًا وفي مزاج سيئ.
questions.explanation_en: Grumpy means in a bad mood.

questions.question: Ms. Weaver wants Pete to be completely ____. (tell the truth)
